newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U Q2 profit rumoured to be 43 cents/share.
newsitem.headline: P&U Q2 profit rumoured to be 43 cents/share.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn was rumoured on Thursday to post a second quarter profit of 43 cents a share, below expectations of 50 cents, market sources told Reuters.
In early trade P&U shares fell as much as 16 crowns but at 1020 GMT they had recovered some ground and were trading eight crowns lower at 264 crowns.
"The rumour says the company will show earnings per share of 43 cents and this is significantly below consensus which is at 50 cents," an analyst said.
Market sources said the information came from P&U sources in the U.S. but no more details were available.
P&U officials here declined to comment on the rumoured figures.
The lower-than-expected second quarter result would reflect tough price competition for the hair loss treatment Rogaine and the stop smoking product Nicorette.
Market rumours said several U.S. players had downgraded their earnings forecasts for P&U which could push the company to issue a further profit warning but the company denied it had such plans.
P&U, which was formed in November 1995 by a merger of U.S.'s Upjohn and Sweden's Pharmacia, has issued three profit warings over the past 12 months.
